_about: Guide format v2 (D-205): quick answer, stat cards, what works / what doesn't, is it right for you, video slot. One entry per guide slug, rendered by GenericPage.astro. Prices, year built and lot size come from src/data/sold/sold-12m.json at build time, not from here. Commute minutes were measured on OpenStreetMap routing (OSRM, no traffic) on the date given. status: draft until Jared approves the verdict and the trade-offs.

murrayville-guide.name: Murrayville
murrayville-guide.summary: Murrayville is the established family neighbourhood on the hill just east of Langley City, with tree-lined streets, sidewalks, Langley Memorial Hospital and the W.C. Blair Recreation Centre, and farmland starting right at its edge.
murrayville-guide.verdict: Pick Murrayville for a quiet, established family street. Look elsewhere if you need a suite to help with the mortgage.
murrayville-guide.vibe: Established and leafy: sidewalks, big trees and family streets, with farm country starting at the edge.

commute.from: Murrayville (OpenStreetMap place point, near 48 Avenue and 216 Street)

works.t: Tree-lined streets with sidewalks, much like Walnut Grove.
Fewer cars parked on the street, because fewer houses have suites.
W.C. Blair Recreation Centre (wave pool, six 25 m lanes, climbing wall) and McLeod Athletic Park (track, lighted turf fields, tennis and pickleball) are in the neighbourhood.
Langley Memorial Hospital, with 24/7 emergency care, is at 22051 Fraser Highway.
Groceries close by: the IGA at 22259 48 Avenue and Ralph’s, plus Shoppers Drug Mart in Murrayville Square.
Bigger lots than the newer suburbs: the typical house that sold sat on about 7,500 square feet.

doesnt.t: Not many houses have a mortgage-helper suite.
Highway 1 is about 12 minutes away off-peak, via 216 Street and Glover Road, farther than from Walnut Grove or Willoughby.
No SkyTrain. The bus to Langley Centre is route 560, and the Langley City SkyTrain extension is expected to open in late 2029.
The hospital’s emergency department and Langley Regional Airport (5385 216 Street) are here. If you’re sensitive to sirens or aircraft, visit the street at a few different times.
Near Murray’s Corner, the heritage conservation area means exterior changes, demolition or subdivision can need a heritage permit.

fit.q: Do you need a basement suite to help pay the mortgage?
fit.a: Then Murrayville makes it harder. Few houses have one. Walnut Grove and Willoughby have more.

fit.q: Do you drive to Surrey or Vancouver most days?
fit.a: Allow about 12 minutes to reach Highway 1 off-peak, 30 minutes to Surrey Central and 54 minutes to downtown Vancouver, before traffic.

fit.q: Would you rather have an established street than a brand-new subdivision?
fit.a: That’s Murrayville’s strength: mature trees, sidewalks and bigger lots. The typical house that sold here was built in 1993.

fit.q: Is a pool, a rec centre and a hospital close by on your list?
fit.a: W.C. Blair, McLeod Athletic Park and Langley Memorial Hospital are all inside the neighbourhood.

faq.q: Is Murrayville a good place to live?
faq.a: For families who want an established street, yes. Murrayville has tree-lined streets with sidewalks, bigger lots, the W.C. Blair Recreation Centre and Langley Memorial Hospital. The trade-offs are few houses with suites and a longer drive to Highway 1 than Walnut Grove or Willoughby.

faq.q: What are the downsides of living in Murrayville?
faq.a: Few houses have a mortgage-helper suite, Highway 1 is about 12 minutes away off-peak, there is no SkyTrain yet, and homes near the hospital or Langley Regional Airport can hear sirens or aircraft. Exterior changes in the heritage area near Murray’s Corner can need a permit.

milner-langley-guide.name: Milner
milner-langley-guide.summary: Milner is the small pocket on the south-east side of Willoughby, by the farmland around Glover Road and 216 Street. A lot of it used to be farmland and one-acre parcels, and it is now a new development area for families and first-time buyers, about five minutes from Highway 1, with farm acreages still on its east side.
milner-langley-guide.verdict: Pick Milner for a newer home in a growing corner of Willoughby, next to the farmland. Look elsewhere if you need shops in walking distance today: they are still coming.
milner-langley-guide.vibe: New homes going in where the farms were, with fields, acreages and a few heritage buildings right next door.

works.t: A good spot for families and first-time home buyers.
More stores and shops are being added, and more development, including stores, is planned at 72 Avenue and 208 Street.
Quick highway access: Highway 1 is about 5 minutes away at the 216 Street interchange.
Fort Langley is about 8 minutes’ drive, and Langley City’s shops are a few minutes the other way.
Room for a farm, horses or a big garden, with Milner Valley Cheese and other farms as neighbours.
A bus on Glover Road: route 562 runs to Langley Centre, Trinity Western University and Carvolth Exchange.
Real history: Milner Station dates to 1910, and the Moir Residence (6840 Glover Road, 1909) is a designated heritage home.

doesnt.t: The stores are coming slowly, so for now most errands are a drive.
It is a development area: expect construction and changing streets nearby for a while.
No public school in the old village: the Milner school has closed, and the closest public elementary is Richard Bulpitt, on 77A Avenue in Willoughby.
No SkyTrain until the Surrey Langley line opens (expected late 2029), and then the nearest station is Langley City Centre.
Many properties run on a well and septic, which need testing and can limit adding bedrooms or a suite.
ALR rules limit subdivision, extra homes and non-farm uses on farm parcels.
Car-first: there is one bus route, and everything else is a drive.

fit.q: Are you a first-time buyer or a young family?
fit.a: That’s who Milner suits: newer homes in a growing part of Willoughby. Check what is planned around the address, because the area is still filling in.

fit.q: Do you want acreage or a small farm?
fit.a: That’s what Milner is for. If the parcel is in the ALR, farming comes first, and subdividing or running a non-farm business needs ALC approval.

fit.q: Do you need a mortgage-helper suite?
fit.a: It depends on the lot. On ALR land a suite has to be inside the main house, though one small additional residence can be allowed, and a septic system has to handle it. For an easy suite, a serviced in-town street is simpler.

fit.q: Do you commute to Surrey or Vancouver?
fit.a: The highway part is easy: about 5 minutes to Highway 1, 22 minutes to Surrey Central and 46 minutes to downtown Vancouver off-peak. There’s no rapid transit until late 2029.

fit.q: Do your kids need a school close by?
fit.a: Check the catchment for the exact address. The old village has no public school; the closest public elementary is Richard Bulpitt (20965 77A Avenue), about a kilometre or two from most of Milner.

faq.q: Is Milner a good place to live?
faq.a: For families and first-time buyers who want a newer home in a growing part of Willoughby, next to the farmland and five minutes from Highway 1, yes. Stores and shops are still being added, so for now most errands are a drive.

faq.q: What are the downsides of living in Milner?
faq.a: Stores and shops are still coming, so errands are a drive for now; construction continues nearby; there is no public school in the old village, no SkyTrain until late 2029, one bus route, many properties on a well and septic, and ALR rules that limit what you can build or subdivide on farm parcels.

salmon-river-guide.name: Salmon River
salmon-river-guide.verdict: Pick Salmon River for elbow room: one-acre communities and bigger lots with room for a shop. Look at Fort Langley instead if you want to walk to the village.
salmon-river-guide.summary: Salmon River is the rural middle of the Township of Langley, between Highway 1 and Fraser Highway from Murrayville east toward Aldergrove, named for the salmon-bearing river that runs north through it to the Fraser at Fort Langley. It is larger-lot houses, acreages and hobby farms on quiet rural roads.
salmon-river-guide.vibe: Elbow room: big yards, shops and paddocks on quiet rural roads, with nothing commercial in the middle of it.

commute.from: the middle of the Salmon River MLS® area

works.t: One-acre communities as well as bigger acreages.
Room to use the land: big yards, space for a shop, and more distance from the neighbours.
Houses sold for about the same median as Fort Langley, but here you are buying the lot, not the walk to the village.
Highway 1 is about 12 minutes from the middle of the area off-peak, and Fort Langley, Murrayville and Aldergrove are the nearby hubs.
Flood works are being upgraded: the Province put $5 million into the Township’s Glen Valley and Salmon River flood project, with more pumping capacity and fish-friendly pumps.

doesnt.t: You drive for most things, and a bigger property takes more work.
Buses run on the edges, not through it: route 562 on Glover Road and route 503 on Fraser Highway.
Many properties run on a well and septic, so testing the well and inspecting the septic are part of every offer.
Creek-side land carries streamside setbacks, and ALR parcels limit subdivision, extra homes and non-farm uses.
Low fields along the river can stay wet after heavy rain; look at the lot in a wet week.

fit.q: Do you want a big yard, a shop or a few animals?
fit.a: That’s what Salmon River is for. Check the zoning and ALR status for what you plan to build or keep before you offer.

fit.q: Do you want to walk to coffee and shops?
fit.a: Then look at Fort Langley village. Salmon River costs about the same for a house, but you’ll drive for errands.

fit.q: Do you commute to Surrey or Vancouver?
fit.a: About 12 minutes to Highway 1, 32 to Surrey Central and 57 to downtown Vancouver off-peak, from the middle of the area. There’s no rapid transit until the Langley SkyTrain opens (expected late 2029).

fit.q: Do you need a mortgage-helper suite?
fit.a: It depends on the lot. On ALR land a suite has to be inside the main house, though one small additional residence can be allowed, and the septic has to handle it. Walnut Grove and Willoughby make a suite simpler.

faq.q: Is Salmon River a good place to live?
faq.a: For buyers who want a big yard, room for a shop or more space between neighbours, yes. Houses sold for about the same median as Fort Langley over the last year. The trade-off is that you drive for most things, and a bigger property takes more work.

faq.q: What are the downsides of living in Salmon River?
faq.a: You drive for most errands, buses only run on the edges, many properties are on a well and septic, creek-side and ALR land come with rules, and low fields can stay wet after heavy rain.

otter-district-guide.name: Otter District
otter-district-guide.verdict: Pick Otter District for more land, close to the Otter Co-op, with room for horses, a shop or a big garden. Look elsewhere if you don’t want weekends of upkeep.
otter-district-guide.summary: Otter District is the south-east corner of the Township of Langley, from Fraser Highway south to the US border between Campbell Valley and Aldergrove. It is working farm country: acreages, horse properties and farms, with the Otter Co-op at 248 Street and Fraser Highway as its local hub.
otter-district-guide.vibe: Flat, open farm country: barns, paddocks and fields on two-lane roads, with the Co-op as the landmark.

commute.from: the middle of the Otter District MLS® area

works.t: More land, and close to the Otter Co-op.
This is where to look if you want to use the land: a few acres for horses, a shop or a big garden.
The Otter Co-op at 248 Street and Fraser Highway, which grew out of the farmers’ institute local farmers formed in 1922, sells groceries, hardware, feed and fuel.
Aldergrove is about 6 minutes away and Highway 1 about 9, from the middle of the district off-peak.
Campbell Valley Regional Park and its horse trails are on the west side of the district.

doesnt.t: A place can look like the perfect horse property until you see what the back field does in November.
Very little comes up for sale: about 20 acreages and manufactured homes sold in a year.
No bus south of Fraser Highway. Route 503 on Fraser Highway is the nearest.
Most properties run on a well and septic, and most of the land is in the ALR, which limits subdivision, extra homes and non-farm uses.
Downtown Vancouver is about an hour off-peak.

fit.q: Are you bringing horses or planning to farm?
fit.a: Then Otter is the right search. Walk the back field after a few days of rain, and check where a dry turnout and hay storage would go.

fit.q: Can you wait for the right property?
fit.a: You may have to. Only a couple of dozen properties sell here in a year, so set up a search and be ready to move.

fit.q: Do you commute west every day?
fit.a: Allow about 36 minutes to Surrey Central and an hour to downtown Vancouver off-peak. Abbotsford and Aldergrove are the easy directions.

fit.q: Do you need a mortgage-helper suite?
fit.a: On ALR land a suite has to be inside the main house, though one small additional residence can be allowed if the Township agrees and the septic can handle it.

faq.q: Is Otter District a good place to live?
faq.a: For buyers who want a few acres for horses, a shop or a big garden and are happy to spend weekends looking after it, yes. Aldergrove is about 6 minutes away and Highway 1 about 9. For transit, walkable shops or plenty of listings to choose from, look in town.

faq.q: What are the downsides of living in Otter District?
faq.a: Wet fields in winter on some properties, very few homes for sale in a year, no bus south of Fraser Highway, wells and septic, ALR rules on most land, and about an hour’s drive to downtown Vancouver.

campbell-valley-guide.name: Campbell Valley
campbell-valley-guide.verdict: Pick Campbell Valley to be close to the horse trails at Campbell Valley Park, with privacy and room for animals. Look elsewhere if you don’t want the upkeep.
campbell-valley-guide.summary: Campbell Valley is south Langley’s valley district, from the Surrey border east to about 232 Street and down to the US border, around Campbell Valley Regional Park and the Little Campbell River. It is acreages, horse properties, vineyards and newer estate houses, with Brookswood at its north edge.
campbell-valley-guide.vibe: Private and green: horse country, farm stands and wineries around a big regional park.

commute.from: the middle of the Campbell Valley MLS® area

works.t: Close to the horse trails in Campbell Valley Park.
Land is the point: fields and animals, without neighbours right on top of you.
Wineries are part of the valley, including Township 7, Chaberton Estate and Vista D’oro.
The Peace Arch crossing is about 21 minutes away off-peak, and White Rock is the nearest beach.
TransLink runs a summer weekend and holiday bus from Langley Centre to the regional park.

doesnt.t: The upkeep. Land takes work.
Groceries are a slightly longer drive, though no worse than from Fort Langley.
Highway 1 is about 16 minutes away off-peak, and there is no weekday bus into the valley.
Very little sells here: about 30 houses and acreages in a year.
Wells and septic on most properties, ALR rules on farm parcels, and streamside setbacks along the Little Campbell River.

fit.q: Do you ride, or want room for animals?
fit.a: This is the valley for it, with the regional park’s horse trails right there. Check the parcel’s ALR status and zoning for barns and arenas.

fit.q: Do you cross the border or head to White Rock often?
fit.a: Then the south end works well: the Peace Arch crossing is about 21 minutes off-peak from the middle of the valley.

fit.q: Do you commute north to Surrey or Vancouver?
fit.a: Allow about 16 minutes to Highway 1, 34 to Surrey Central and 59 to downtown Vancouver off-peak.

fit.q: Would you rather have a yard than acreage?
fit.a: Brookswood, at the valley’s north edge, gives you big lots with Township services.

faq.q: Is Campbell Valley a good place to live?
faq.a: For acreage buyers who want privacy and room for horses, a shop or a big garden, yes, with the regional park at its heart. The trade-offs are the upkeep, a longer drive for groceries and Highway 1, and very few homes for sale.

faq.q: What are the downsides of living in Campbell Valley?
faq.a: Land takes upkeep, groceries and Highway 1 are a longer drive, there is no weekday bus, very little comes up for sale, and wells, septic, ALR rules and river setbacks apply to many properties.

county-line-glen-valley-guide.name: County Line / Glen Valley
county-line-glen-valley-guide.verdict: Pick Glen Valley for more hills and privacy, closer to Fort Langley. Look elsewhere if a low, wet lot or a steep driveway would bother you.
county-line-glen-valley-guide.summary: County Line / Glen Valley is the north-east corner of the Township of Langley, from east of Fort Langley to the Abbotsford line, with farm flats along the Fraser River and higher land on the slope behind. It is farms and acreages, most of it in the ALR, with Glen Valley Regional Park on the river.
county-line-glen-valley-guide.vibe: Quiet farm country toward the Fraser: river flats, berry fields and acreages on the slope.

commute.from: the middle of the County Line Glen Valley MLS® area

works.t: More hills, and closer to Fort Langley.
Privacy, and the river side is beautiful.
Glen Valley Regional Park is on the Fraser, with river fishing and riverside trails.
Highway 1 is about 9 minutes from the middle of the area off-peak, and Fort Langley about 15.
The Province put $5 million into the Township’s Glen Valley and Salmon River flood project: pump capacity, dike bank repairs, culverts and ditches.

doesnt.t: Low, wet land on the flats and higher land with a steeper driveway are two very different places to live.
The flats sit beside the Fraser, which rises in the spring freshet. Check the flood mapping for the address and get an insurance quote early.
Very little sells: about 17 acreages in a year.
No bus in the valley, and no shops or school in it; Fort Langley and Aldergrove are the hubs.
Wells, septic and ALR rules on most properties, and farm traffic on the roads.

fit.q: Do you want land near the river?
fit.a: Then drive down toward Glen Valley Regional Park first, and decide between the flats and the slope before you look at houses.

fit.q: Would a flood risk keep you up at night?
fit.a: Then stay on the higher ground on the slope, and check the flood mapping and insurance for any address on the flats.

fit.q: Do you commute to Surrey or Vancouver?
fit.a: About 9 minutes to Highway 1, 30 to Surrey Central and 54 to downtown Vancouver off-peak, from the middle of the area.

fit.q: Do you want to walk to a village?
fit.a: Then look at Fort Langley itself, about 15 minutes west.

faq.q: Is County Line / Glen Valley a good place to live?
faq.a: For acreage buyers who want privacy and like being out toward the Fraser River, yes. Highway 1 is about 9 minutes away. The big choice is between the low river flats and the higher land on the slope, which live very differently.

faq.q: What are the downsides of living in Glen Valley?
faq.a: The river flats can flood in a big spring freshet, very little comes up for sale, there is no bus, shop or school in the valley, and wells, septic and ALR rules apply to most properties.

port-kells-surrey-guide.name: Port Kells
port-kells-surrey-guide.summary: Port Kells is Surrey’s north-east corner, on the Fraser River at the Langley border. North of Highway 1 it is an established industrial area of about 781 acres and roughly 610 businesses, mostly light industrial. South of the highway is the original village: a school, a park with an outdoor pool and homes on large rural lots.
port-kells-surrey-guide.verdict: Pick Port Kells for a business that runs on Highway 1. Look elsewhere if you want a regular neighbourhood with listings to choose from.
port-kells-surrey-guide.vibe: Warehouses, truck yards and freight trains north of the highway; a quiet village with big treed lots and farmland south of it.

works.t: Highway 1 and the Golden Ears Bridge are close by.
There’s some farmland, and the village has an elementary school and a park with an outdoor pool. Walnut Grove’s shops are a few minutes away.
An established industrial area: about 781 acres and roughly 610 businesses, so your suppliers, trades and customers are close by.
Surrey had more commercial sales than any other Fraser Valley city in the second quarter of 2026 (53, 19 of them industrial).
Surrey’s industrial vacancy was 4.2% in the third quarter, lower than Langley’s 5.7%.
A bus for staff: TransLink’s 501 runs along 96 Avenue to Surrey Central and Langley Centre.

doesnt.t: Not much choice: four detached listings and no sales in September 2026.
Expect truck and rail traffic, and use 200 Street to get onto Highway 1 eastbound.
The river frontage has no dyke, so flood construction levels apply to building there.
Trans Mountain’s pipeline and pump station are in the district: work within 30 m of the pipeline needs the company’s written consent.
Lots of new supply: Surrey has 1.6 million sq ft of industrial space under construction, so landlords compete for tenants.
Port Kells-specific development cost charges if you build or expand.
No SkyTrain until late 2029, and then Clayton Station is a drive away.

fit.q: Are you buying a building for your own business?
fit.a: Port Kells is built for it: highway access, other industrial businesses around you and a bus for staff. Before you firm up, check that your use is permitted on the exact property, the flood construction level, the site’s past uses and any pipeline or rail line nearby.

fit.q: Are you buying to lease it out?
fit.a: Look hard at the supply. Surrey vacancy was 4.2% in the third quarter, but 1.6 million sq ft is under construction and more space was given back than leased, so price the rent you expect against new buildings nearby.

fit.q: Do your trucks run east and west on Highway 1?
fit.a: Westbound is easy from 192 Street. Eastbound goes through the 200 Street interchange, a few minutes further. North over the Golden Ears Bridge is straight up 96 Avenue and Golden Ears Way.

fit.q: Do you want to live near your work?
fit.a: Then look south of the highway, in the village, where homes sit on large lots. The industrial lots are for business. Very little comes up for sale, so tell me early and I’ll watch for it.

fit.q: Do you want a regular neighbourhood with shops and listings to choose from?
fit.a: Then Port Kells isn’t it. Clayton, Fleetwood and Walnut Grove are close and have the choice.

faq.q: Is Port Kells industrial or residential?
faq.a: Both, split by Highway 1. North of the highway it is an industrial area of about 781 acres and roughly 610 businesses, mostly light industrial. South of it is the old village and rural homes on large lots, with ALR farmland along the southern edge.

faq.q: Is Port Kells in a floodplain?
faq.a: The river frontage is. The City says the Fraser River frontage east of 132 Street to the Langley border has no dyke, and development there had to be built to flood protection levels. Ask the City for the flood construction level for the exact property.

faq.q: How much does industrial property cost in Port Kells?
faq.a: No one publishes a Port Kells price on its own. Across Surrey, asking industrial rents averaged $19.66 a square foot net plus $6.95 additional rent in the third quarter of 2026. Sale prices depend on the building, the land and the zoning, so ask Jared for recent comparable sales.

abbotsford-east-guide.name: Abbotsford East
abbotsford-east-guide.verdict: Abbotsford East suits families looking for a detached home, a yard and parks nearby. Hilly streets: expect stairs, sloped yards and driving for most errands, with limited bus service.

abbotsford-west-guide.name: Abbotsford West
abbotsford-west-guide.verdict: Abbotsford West suits families who want more bedrooms and anyone who regularly drives west toward Langley. The catch is that some homes have a lot of square footage spread over levels that may or may not work for your family.

aberdeen-guide.name: Aberdeen
aberdeen-guide.verdict: Aberdeen suits families who want a detached house on the west side of Abbotsford and buyers looking for more room outside. Out on a rural road, expect more driving and more upkeep.

albion-guide.name: Albion
albion-guide.verdict: Albion suits families moving up to a bigger townhome or a detached house. The catch is that getting out to Lougheed can take longer than you’d guess from the map.

aldergrove-guide.name: Aldergrove
aldergrove-guide.verdict: Aldergrove suits buyers who want a detached house with a yard, especially if you’re moving up from a townhome. The catch is the commute.

annieville-guide.name: Annieville
annieville-guide.verdict: Annieville suits buyers looking for an older detached house, a proper yard and a quieter side street. The catch is that two houses built around the same time can have very different maintenance histories.

auguston-abbotsford-guide.name: Auguston
auguston-abbotsford-guide.verdict: Auguston suits families who want a serviced house on the Sumas Mountain bench. The catch is the City’s McKee Neighbourhood Plan, adopted in 2023, plans more homes and schools on this slope, so you’re buying into a neighbourhood that’s still growing.

beach-grove-guide.name: Beach Grove
beach-grove-guide.verdict: Beach Grove suits buyers who want a quieter coastal neighbourhood and would actually use the dike for walks. The catch is that with an older place near the bay, I’d want to understand how the property handles wet weather.

bear-creek-green-timbers-guide.name: Bear Creek / Green Timbers
bear-creek-green-timbers-guide.verdict: Bear Creek / Green Timbers suits families who want a yard and somewhere nearby to walk the dog or take the kids. Mostly 1980s homes, some really priced as lot value, and most sellers took under asking.

bolivar-heights-guide.name: Bolivar Heights
bolivar-heights-guide.verdict: Bolivar Heights suits buyers who want a detached home and like the idea of a view or a bit more separation from the neighbours. A great view can come with less flat, usable yard than you’d think.

boundary-beach-guide.name: Boundary Beach
boundary-beach-guide.verdict: Boundary Beach suits people who’ll use the beach year-round and are happy to drive into town for most errands. The catch is that I’d want to understand flood exposure and insurance for the exact address early on.

bradner-guide.name: Bradner
bradner-guide.verdict: Bradner suits buyers who want acreage and like living in a farming community. The catch is that farm country comes with early starts, equipment on the road and the odd day when you’ll smell what’s happening next door.

bridal-falls-guide.name: Bridal Falls
bridal-falls-guide.verdict: Bridal Falls suits buyers who want a foothills setting, especially if they’re looking for a recreational place. The catch is that if you’re looking at Bridal Falls RV Resort, what you can put on the lot and how you can use it are things I’d check before comparing it with a regular house.

works.t: Bridal Veil Falls Provincial Park next door, with its 60 m waterfall.
Quick access to Highway 1 and the bridge north to Agassiz.

doesnt.t: At the RV resort, what you can put on a lot and how you can use it are limited.
Transit is on request only (route 71).

bridgeview-guide.name: Bridgeview
bridgeview-guide.verdict: Bridgeview suits buyers who want a detached house and would make regular use of Scott Road SkyTrain station. The catch is that there are designated floodplain areas, so I’d look at the exact address before getting too attached to a house.

brookswood-guide.name: Brookswood
brookswood-guide.verdict: Brookswood suits young families. The catch is that most of the older lots are on septic.

cedar-hills-guide.name: Cedar Hills
cedar-hills-guide.verdict: Cedar Hills suits buyers who want a detached house with a yard and are happy to update it over time. The catch is that the money you set aside for a kitchen can disappear fast if the roof or drainage needs attention first.

central-abbotsford-guide.name: Central Abbotsford
central-abbotsford-guide.verdict: Central Abbotsford suits first-time condo buyers and downsizers who want errands and a good walking loop nearby. The catch with an older condo is that a nice unit can come with a long list of building repairs.

central-meadows-pitt-meadows-guide.name: Central Meadows
central-meadows-pitt-meadows-guide.verdict: Central Meadows suits first-time buyers and downsizers who want flatter streets, shops nearby and the option of taking the train. The catch is that living near the tracks and living a few blocks back can feel quite different.

chilliwack-downtown-guide.name: Chilliwack Downtown
chilliwack-downtown-guide.verdict: Chilliwack Downtown suits first-time condo buyers and anyone who likes walking out for coffee or dinner. The catch is that the same street you like on a Saturday afternoon might feel busier than you want when you’re trying to sleep.

chilliwack-mountain-guide.name: Chilliwack Mountain
chilliwack-mountain-guide.verdict: Chilliwack Mountain suits buyers who want a river or valley view and are happy to drive into town. Big views, but it's hill driving with almost no bus service, and detached listings have been sitting a while.

chilliwack-proper-east-guide.name: Chilliwack Proper East
chilliwack-proper-east-guide.verdict: Chilliwack Proper East suits buyers who’d take an older detached home with a yard and do some work over time. Older homes near downtown, many sold as investor or redevelopment plays; expect updates and nearby infill.

chilliwack-proper-south-guide.name: Chilliwack Proper South
chilliwack-proper-south-guide.verdict: Chilliwack Proper South suits first-time condo buyers and people who want to stay central with a straightforward drive to work or errands. Check which way a unit faces: two units in the same building can feel completely different with the windows open.

chilliwack-proper-west-guide.name: Chilliwack Proper West
chilliwack-proper-west-guide.verdict: Chilliwack Proper West suits first-time buyers looking for a condo or an older house close to town. Lots of older condos, 55+ and manufactured-home parks; most sales closed a bit under asking.

river-valley-guide.name: Chilliwack River Valley
river-valley-guide.verdict: Chilliwack River Valley suits people who fish, hike or spend a lot of time outdoors and are happy living farther from town. The catch is that on a river-valley property, I’d care just as much about the road home and how the lot handles high water as I would about the house itself.

clayton-guide.name: Clayton
clayton-guide.verdict: Clayton suits buyers who want a newer townhome and like being able to walk to a park or grab coffee. Dense and newer, with small lots, tandem garages and tight street parking.

cliff-drive-guide.name: Cliff Drive
cliff-drive-guide.verdict: Cliff Drive suits families looking for a detached home on an established street and buyers who’d consider a hillside property for the outlook. If the house is on a slope, the catch is how much that can change your day-to-day use of the yard and driveway.

cloverdale-bc-guide.name: Cloverdale
cloverdale-bc-guide.verdict: Cloverdale suits buyers who want a detached house with a proper backyard and a quieter street. The catch is that some of the homes with the best yards are older.

columbia-valley-guide.name: Columbia Valley
columbia-valley-guide.verdict: Columbia Valley suits buyers who want acreage and quiet and are happy living beyond Cultus Lake. The catch is that a quick errand can turn into a proper drive, especially when the lake is busy.

cottonwood-maple-ridge-guide.name: Cottonwood
cottonwood-maple-ridge-guide.verdict: Cottonwood suits families moving up to a bigger townhome or detached house. Still filling in, with ongoing townhouse and infill building, tandem garages and smaller lots.

crescent-beach-ocean-park-guide.name: Crescent Beach
crescent-beach-ocean-park-guide.verdict: Crescent Beach suits someone who’ll actually use the beach. The catch is that sunny summer weekends get busy.

cultus-lake-guide.name: Cultus Lake
cultus-lake-guide.verdict: Cultus Lake suits buyers who’ll use the lake regularly, whether they’re looking for a weekend place or somewhere to live year-round. The catch is summer traffic and, for homes on Cultus Lake Park residential leases, getting clear on the lease before you compare prices.

delta-manor-guide.name: Delta Manor
delta-manor-guide.verdict: Delta Manor suits first-time buyers looking at townhomes and buyers who want to stay central without paying for a big house. The catch is that two townhomes at the same price can come with very different repair bills down the road.

dewdney-deroche-mission-guide.name: Dewdney / Deroche
dewdney-deroche-mission-guide.verdict: Dewdney / Deroche suits buyers who want a rural house or some land east of Mission and are fine driving into town. The catch is that a place on the Lougheed and one farther off it can feel completely different, even if they’re only a few minutes apart.

durieu-mission-guide.name: Durieu
durieu-mission-guide.verdict: Durieu suits buyers who want a small acreage or a country house in the Hatzic Valley. The catch is that where the house sits in the valley matters.

east-central-maple-ridge-guide.name: East Central Maple Ridge
east-central-maple-ridge-guide.verdict: East Central Maple Ridge suits first-time buyers open to a townhome or an older detached house they can improve over time. The catch is that the walk into town varies a lot by address.

east-chilliwack-guide.name: East Chilliwack
east-chilliwack-guide.verdict: East Chilliwack suits families who want a detached house with room outside and don’t mind driving into town. The catch is that a road can feel quiet from the backyard and still be awkward to walk along with kids.

east-delta-guide.name: East Delta
east-delta-guide.verdict: East Delta suits buyers who want to be in working farm country and are comfortable driving for most errands. The catch is that life on a farm road comes with trucks, equipment and neighbours who start work early.

works.t: Open farm country between the south arm of the Fraser and Boundary Bay, right next to Surrey.
Wide open, especially along 104 Street.

doesnt.t: Farm roads come with trucks, equipment and neighbours who start work early.
It is diked floodplain: ask what dike protects the property and get insurance quotes early.

east-newton-guide.name: East Newton
east-newton-guide.verdict: East Newton suits buyers who want a yard and are open to an older detached house. Older complexes, many of them 55+; detached homes have sat longer and mostly sold under asking.

eastern-hillsides-guide.name: Eastern Hillsides
eastern-hillsides-guide.verdict: Eastern Hillsides suits buyers who want a view, a quieter setting and are happy driving into town. Hillside living means driving for everything; plenty of new lots for sale, and some have sold as court-ordered sales.

elgin-chantrell-guide.name: Elgin Chantrell
elgin-chantrell-guide.verdict: Elgin Chantrell suits families who want room for the kids to play, or anyone who wants a bit more space between neighbours. The catch is that you’ll drive for most errands, and a bigger yard means more upkeep.

english-bluff-guide.name: English Bluff
english-bluff-guide.verdict: English Bluff suits buyers who want a water view or a quieter coastal setting and are comfortable looking after a more involved property. The catch is that if the house sits near the bluff, I’d want to know how the lot drains and what reports exist before falling for the view.

fairfield-island-guide.name: Fairfield Island
fairfield-island-guide.verdict: Fairfield Island suits families who want a detached house, a yard and quieter streets close to town. The catch is that on a low-lying lot, I’d want to know how it drains and whether there’s been water in the house.

fleetwood-tynehead-guide.name: Fleetwood / Tynehead
fleetwood-tynehead-guide.verdict: Fleetwood / Tynehead suits families looking for a townhome or detached house with a bit more space. The catch is that getting onto Fraser Highway or out to Highway 1 can be a different story at rush hour.

fort-langley-guide.name: Fort Langley
fort-langley-guide.verdict: Fort Langley suits young families, retirees, people who want a character home and anyone who doesn’t want too much development and wants to be by the river. The catch is price.

fraser-heights-guide.name: Fraser Heights
fraser-heights-guide.verdict: Fraser Heights suits families who want a detached house and expect to spend a lot of their week close to home. The catch is that getting onto Highway 1 at the wrong time can change your commute pretty quickly.

garrison-crossing-guide.name: Garrison Crossing
garrison-crossing-guide.verdict: Garrison Crossing suits downsizers and families who want to walk for coffee, groceries or a swim. The catch is that the homes can feel close together, especially if you’re coming from a place with a big yard.

grandview-heights-guide.name: Grandview Heights
grandview-heights-guide.verdict: Grandview Heights suits young families, professionals and investors. The catch is that it can have traffic sometimes because of all the construction.

greendale-guide.name: Greendale
greendale-guide.verdict: Greendale suits buyers who want flat land and a country feel on the west side of Chilliwack. The catch is that a flat field can stay wet long after the yard around the house has dried out.

guildford-guide.name: Guildford
guildford-guide.verdict: Guildford suits first-time buyers and downsizers who want shopping and transit close by. The catch is that a place facing 104th can feel very different from one tucked inside the same complex.

hatzic-mission-guide.name: Hatzic
hatzic-mission-guide.verdict: Hatzic suits buyers who want a view, a bigger yard or somewhere that feels a little removed from town. The catch is that an uphill address and a low-lying one are very different purchases, so I’d look at the lot as closely as the house.

hawthorne-guide.name: Hawthorne
hawthorne-guide.verdict: Hawthorne suits families looking for a detached house with a yard and a school close by. The catch is that a place right on 56th can feel a lot busier than one around the corner.

hazelmere-guide.name: Hazelmere
hazelmere-guide.verdict: Hazelmere suits buyers who want room for horses, a shop, a big garden, or just enough space for the kids to run around, without neighbours close by. The catch is maintaining the property, but you also get fields.

hemlock-valley-mission-guide.name: Hemlock Valley
hemlock-valley-mission-guide.verdict: Hemlock Valley suits skiers, snowboarders and buyers who’ll get enough use out of a mountain place to make it worthwhile. The catch is getting up there on a snowy Friday night.

works.t: A mountain resort community: weekends at Sasquatch Mountain.
35 named trails on the south and southwest slopes.

doesnt.t: Getting up there on a snowy Friday night.
One road in and out: the road up from Harrison Mills is also the evacuation route.

holly-guide.name: Holly
holly-guide.verdict: Holly suits families who want a detached house, a backyard and an easy route out toward Highway 99. The trade-off is driving into the village more often.

king-george-corridor-guide.name: King George Corridor
king-george-corridor-guide.verdict: King George Corridor suits buyers who want to stay in South Surrey and have more condo and townhome options. The catch is traffic noise.

ladner-elementary-guide.name: Ladner Elementary
ladner-elementary-guide.verdict: Ladner Elementary suits families who want to walk to school and anyone who likes being close to the village. Low-lying behind the dikes, near the river and farmland, with older detached homes and higher strata fees.

ladner-rural-guide.name: Ladner Rural
ladner-rural-guide.verdict: Ladner Rural suits buyers who want a country property but still want Ladner Village to be part of their everyday life. The catch is that acreage listings can make every outbuilding sound useful.

works.t: Working farms and waterfront along the Fraser River and River Road West.
Quiet country living, a few minutes from Ladner Village.

doesnt.t: The lowland is diked floodplain, and the flood construction level is set parcel by parcel.
ALR rules decide what you can build, split or run on the land.

lake-errock-mission-guide.name: Lake Errock
lake-errock-mission-guide.verdict: Lake Errock suits buyers who want a quieter place near the lake and are comfortable being farther from everyday services. The catch is that “near the lake” can mean a lot of things.

langley-city-guide.name: Langley City
langley-city-guide.verdict: Langley City suits first-time condo buyers, and anyone who wants to walk to grab coffee, groceries or dinner. SkyTrain construction is part of the catch right now, but the building and your daily route are what I’d focus on.

little-mountain-guide.name: Little Mountain
little-mountain-guide.verdict: Little Mountain suits buyers who want a view or a hillside setting and still want to be close to town. Older homes on bigger lots, and few sales, so prices are harder to read.

lower-landing-guide.name: Lower Landing
lower-landing-guide.verdict: Lower Landing suits buyers looking for a newer townhome or detached home, especially if Cedarbrook is on their list. The catch is that Lower Landing is an MLS label, and Cedarbrook’s project documents describe a leasehold land arrangement.

majuba-hill-guide.name: Majuba Hill
majuba-hill-guide.verdict: Majuba Hill suits buyers who want a large-lot rural home above Yarrow. The catch is there’s only one road in and out, Yarrow Central Road, and trail users heading up Vedder Mountain use it too.

matsqui-guide.name: Matsqui
matsqui-guide.verdict: Matsqui suits buyers who like an older village setting or want land in an established farming area. On the low ground, the catch I’d look into early is flood exposure.

mid-meadows-pitt-meadows-guide.name: Mid Meadows
mid-meadows-pitt-meadows-guide.verdict: Mid Meadows suits first-time buyers and downsizers who want a condo or townhome close to shopping. The catch is that you’re near Lougheed, so I’d care a lot about which way the unit faces.

mission-bc-mission-guide.name: Mission
mission-bc-mission-guide.verdict: Mission suits buyers who want a detached house with a yard and have some flexibility on where or when they commute. Long commute west. The West Coast Express runs weekdays only, into Vancouver in the morning and back in the evening, and homes take longer to sell.

mission-west-mission-guide.name: Mission West
mission-west-mission-guide.verdict: Mission West suits buyers who want elbow room and are comfortable driving for most things. The catch is that if you’re buying for the quiet, it’s worth finding out what’s planned around you.

morgan-creek-guide.name: Morgan Creek
morgan-creek-guide.verdict: Morgan Creek suits downsizers and families. The catch is that a lot of the bigger estate homes around $2M to $2.5M need updating.

neilsen-grove-guide.name: Neilsen Grove
neilsen-grove-guide.verdict: Neilsen Grove suits downsizers who want somewhere flat to walk and families who like the quieter north end of Ladner. The catch is that if you picture yourself popping into the village on foot every day, the north end may feel a little farther out than you want.

nordel-guide.name: Nordel
nordel-guide.verdict: Nordel suits families who want an established detached neighbourhood and often drive toward Highway 91. Right on Nordel Way it’s busy, so look a few turns off it.

north-maple-ridge-guide.name: North Maple Ridge
north-maple-ridge-guide.verdict: North Maple Ridge suits buyers who want a bigger lot, more trees and some space between neighbours. The catch is that a long driveway and a treed lot are both things you’ll have to look after.

north-meadows-pitt-meadows-guide.name: North Meadows
north-meadows-pitt-meadows-guide.verdict: North Meadows suits acreage buyers who like open views and want room for a garden, animals or equipment. The catch with a low, flat property is that drainage can make a big difference to how much land you can use through the year.

northeast-maple-ridge-guide.name: Northeast Maple Ridge
northeast-maple-ridge-guide.verdict: Northeast Maple Ridge suits acreage buyers who want room on the rural east side. The catch is you’re out on the rural east side: Kanaka Creek cuts through with only a few bridge crossings, and you’re farther from the town centre.

northwest-maple-ridge-guide.name: Northwest Maple Ridge
northwest-maple-ridge-guide.verdict: Northwest Maple Ridge suits families who want a detached house and regularly head west toward Pitt Meadows or the Tri-Cities. Mostly 1980s homes, and most commutes are by car over the Golden Ears Bridge or along Lougheed.

pacific-douglas-guide.name: Pacific Douglas
pacific-douglas-guide.verdict: Pacific Douglas suits buyers who want a newer house or townhome in a quieter part of South Surrey. The catch is you’ll probably drive for groceries, coffee, and most errands.

panorama-ridge-guide.name: Panorama Ridge
panorama-ridge-guide.verdict: Panorama Ridge suits buyers who want more privacy, mature trees and a yard they’ll spend time in. Car-first suburb off Highway 10 and Scott Road; many homes are from the 1990s and due for updates.

popkum-guide.name: Popkum
popkum-guide.verdict: Popkum suits buyers who want a detached home on the east side of Chilliwack and like having a quieter place to come home to. The catch is that you’re still heading out for a lot of your errands, and how close you are to Highway 1 can change how quiet the yard feels.

poplar-guide.name: Poplar
poplar-guide.verdict: Poplar suits first-time condo buyers who want to be near UFV and buyers who need easy Highway 1 access. The catch is that an event night can feel different from a normal Tuesday, especially for parking.

port-guichon-guide.name: Port Guichon
port-guichon-guide.verdict: Port Guichon suits buyers who want Ladner’s river side and like being close to the village. “Waterfront” can mean very different properties here, so check what the listing means.

promontory-guide.name: Promontory
promontory-guide.verdict: Promontory suits buyers who want a family-sized house or townhome and like the idea of a view or trails nearby. The catch is the hill.

queen-mary-park-surrey-guide.name: Queen Mary Park
queen-mary-park-surrey-guide.verdict: Queen Mary Park suits buyers who want a yard and an established street without being far from central Surrey. The catch is that the busier roads can be close enough to hear from the backyard.

rosedale-guide.name: Rosedale
rosedale-guide.verdict: Rosedale suits buyers who want a smaller community, a bigger yard or an acreage on the east side of Chilliwack. The catch is that a house close to the school and an acreage farther out can come with very different upkeep.

rosemary-heights-guide.name: Rosemary Heights
rosemary-heights-guide.verdict: Rosemary Heights suits families who want parks and schools nearby, and buyers who want a townhome with a bit more room. The catch is you’ll still drive for most of those errands.

royal-heights-guide.name: Royal Heights
royal-heights-guide.verdict: Royal Heights suits buyers looking for an older detached house with a yard who regularly head toward North Delta or New West. The catch is that some lots have a fair bit of slope, so the yard can look bigger on paper than it feels in person.

ryder-lake-guide.name: Ryder Lake
ryder-lake-guide.verdict: Ryder Lake suits buyers who want privacy, views and some land and are happy to be up out of town. Rural acreages up the hill with no bus service; ask about water, septic and road access before you offer.

sardis-east-vedder-guide.name: Sardis East Vedder
sardis-east-vedder-guide.verdict: Sardis East Vedder suits families and downsizers who want flatter streets and an established neighbourhood. The catch is that some of the older homes need work even when they show well.

sardis-south-guide.name: Sardis South
sardis-south-guide.verdict: Sardis South suits families and downsizers who want flatter streets and easy access to outdoor space. The catch is that access to shops and the trail can feel different depending on which side of Vedder Road you’re on.

sardis-west-vedder-guide.name: Sardis West Vedder
sardis-west-vedder-guide.verdict: Sardis West Vedder suits families who want a townhome or detached house and drive west on Highway 1 regularly. The catch is that the closer you get to the busy routes, the more I’d pay attention to what you can hear from the yard.

scottsdale-guide.name: Scottsdale
scottsdale-guide.verdict: Scottsdale suits buyers who want groceries, restaurants and transit close by. The catch is that the convenience comes with traffic, especially if your place faces the main road.

serpentine-guide.name: Serpentine
serpentine-guide.verdict: Serpentine suits buyers who want land for horses, farming or a shop and still want to be close to Cloverdale. That’s the catch I’d pay attention to on the Serpentine flats.

works.t: Commercial and industrial listings come up around 184 Street and 32 Avenue.
A mix of farmland and work land that suits farmers and industrial companies.

doesnt.t: Much of the lowland is floodplain close to sea level, managed by sea dams, dikes and pump stations.
Ground that is soggy half the year is worth less than its acreage suggests.

silver-valley-guide.name: Silver Valley
silver-valley-guide.verdict: Silver Valley suits buyers who want a newer family home and would rather have trees and trails nearby than walk to the shops. The catch is that school, groceries and everything else can turn into a drive, and some yards are smaller or steeper than the house photos suggest.

south-meadows-pitt-meadows-guide.name: South Meadows
south-meadows-pitt-meadows-guide.verdict: South Meadows suits families and downsizers who want flat streets and somewhere good to walk or ride a bike. The catch is that you can be close to a great walking route and still need the car for a full grocery run.

southwest-maple-ridge-guide.name: Southwest Maple Ridge
southwest-maple-ridge-guide.verdict: Southwest Maple Ridge suits buyers who want an older detached house and like being on the west side for trips toward Pitt Meadows or across the Golden Ears Bridge. The catch is that if you’re near the rail line, train noise can matter more than you’d think on a quick showing.

stave-falls-mission-guide.name: Stave Falls
stave-falls-mission-guide.verdict: Stave Falls suits buyers who want trees, privacy and somewhere that feels rural when they get home. The catch is that on a more tucked-away road, I’d check what internet you can actually get and how much driveway you’ll be looking after.

steelhead-mission-guide.name: Steelhead
steelhead-mission-guide.verdict: Steelhead suits buyers who want a treed acreage and like being tucked away. The catch is that something as simple as getting reliable internet can become an address-by-address question.

sullivan-station-guide.name: Sullivan Station
sullivan-station-guide.verdict: Sullivan Station suits families moving up from a condo who want another bedroom and a park nearby. Mostly newer townhomes with tandem garages; detached lots are small and slower to sell.

sumas-mountain-guide.name: Sumas Mountain
sumas-mountain-guide.verdict: Sumas Mountain suits buyers who want trees, trails and a bit of separation from town. The catch is that the hill becomes part of the routine, from driving home to finding a flat spot for the kids to play.

works.t: Trails at your door: the hike past Chadsey Lake to the top looks out over the Fraser Valley.
Trees, and a bit of separation from town.

doesnt.t: The hill is part of the routine, from steep driveways to finding a flat spot for the kids to play.
Gravel trucks from the mountain’s quarries use an access road to Highway 1.

sumas-prairie-guide.name: Sumas Prairie
sumas-prairie-guide.verdict: Sumas Prairie suits buyers who need real working land or want an acreage in an active farming area. The catch is flood exposure, and that would be one of my first questions on any property I liked.

sunnyside-park-surrey-guide.name: Sunnyside Park
sunnyside-park-surrey-guide.verdict: Sunnyside Park suits families who want an established neighbourhood and downsizers who want errands close by. Mostly older complexes, many 55+, with higher strata fees; nearly all sales closed under asking.

sunshine-hills-woods-guide.name: Sunshine Hills / Woods
sunshine-hills-woods-guide.verdict: Sunshine Hills / Woods suits families who want a treed neighbourhood and anyone who’d use the trails regularly. The catch is that a shaded yard can stay damp and get less light than you expect.

thornhill-maple-ridge-guide.name: Thornhill
thornhill-maple-ridge-guide.verdict: Thornhill suits buyers who want a treed lot, more privacy and trails nearby. Part rural: acreages on septic, very few buses, and homes have taken longer to sell.

tsawwassen-central-guide.name: Tsawwassen Central
tsawwassen-central-guide.verdict: Tsawwassen Central suits downsizers who want to stay close to town and families looking for an established street. The catch is that a place close to the shops can still involve a walk you’d rarely do, depending on the route.

tsawwassen-east-guide.name: Tsawwassen East
tsawwassen-east-guide.verdict: Tsawwassen East suits families looking for an established detached neighbourhood and buyers who’d rather have a yard than be right in the middle of town. The catch is that some homes sit on a slope, and the walk home can feel quite different from the walk out.

tsawwassen-north-guide.name: Tsawwassen North
tsawwassen-north-guide.verdict: Tsawwassen North suits downsizers who like the Springs and buyers looking for a newer condo or townhome near the shops. The big catch is that ownership can vary by development, including leasehold homes on Tsawwassen First Nation lands.

vedder-crossing-guide.name: Vedder Crossing
vedder-crossing-guide.verdict: Vedder Crossing suits buyers who want a condo or townhome near everyday shops and would use the river trails. The catch is that being close to Vedder Road can mean more traffic noise, and the walk to the trail depends on which side you’re on.

vedder-mountain-guide.name: Vedder Mountain
vedder-mountain-guide.verdict: Vedder Mountain suits buyers who want a treed hillside setting and are happy driving for groceries and school. The catch is that on a hillside lot, a big backyard on the listing can turn out to be mostly slope.

walnut-grove-guide.name: Walnut Grove
walnut-grove-guide.verdict: Walnut Grove suits families who want to be close to Highway 1. The catch is that some lots are smaller, closer to 5,000 or 6,000 sq ft, but you’ll also find homes with suites.

websters-corners-guide.name: Websters Corners
websters-corners-guide.verdict: Websters Corners suits buyers who want a bigger lot, more privacy and a more rural feel. The catch is that a big lot takes work, and if the property uses a well or septic system, those become part of what you’re buying.

west-central-maple-ridge-guide.name: West Central Maple Ridge
west-central-maple-ridge-guide.verdict: West Central Maple Ridge suits condo buyers, downsizers and people who want shops and services within walking distance. The catch is that traffic and street noise come with some of that convenience.

west-chilliwack-guide.name: West Chilliwack
west-chilliwack-guide.verdict: West Chilliwack suits buyers who want a rural property, including 55+ downsizers. The catch is it’s planned under the City’s Agricultural Area Plan, so check what that plan and the ALR allow on the exact parcel.

works.t: Rural property on the agricultural west side of the city, from Village West to Chilliwack Mountain.
Popular with 55+ downsizers from the Valley and the coast.

doesnt.t: The Agricultural Area Plan and the ALR decide what you can do with the land.
Flood setbacks: buildings must sit 60 m from the Fraser and 75 m from the Vedder River.

west-meadows-pitt-meadows-guide.name: West Meadows
west-meadows-pitt-meadows-guide.verdict: West Meadows suits buyers who want open space and are comfortable living near farmland and the airport. The catch is that aircraft noise is easy to miss if your showing happens during a quiet stretch.

works.t: A quiet residential area on the west side of Pitt Meadows, with detached homes, townhouses and estate properties.
More room and open views.

doesnt.t: Aircraft noise from the airport, easy to miss on a quiet showing.
City transit centres on the West Coast Express station in the urban core, not the rural areas.

west-newton-guide.name: West Newton
west-newton-guide.verdict: West Newton suits families who want more bedrooms or space for parents under one roof. The catch is that some streets are already packed with cars by the time everyone gets home.

westham-island-guide.name: Westham Island
westham-island-guide.verdict: Westham Island suits buyers who want a genuine farming setting and are happy with a quieter, more out-of-the-way routine. The catch is that the bridge is part of every trip into town, whether you’re grabbing milk or bringing home a load of hay.

works.t: Farm fields and marsh out toward the Reifel bird sanctuary.
More than 700 hectares of ALR farmland: a real farming setting.

doesnt.t: The bridge is part of every trip into town.
It sits on the Fraser estuary: check flood status and insurance before you remove subjects.

whalley-guide.name: Whalley
whalley-guide.verdict: Whalley suits first-time condo buyers and anyone who wants to commute by SkyTrain. The catch is that a condo facing King George can feel a lot busier than one a block back.

white-rock-guide.name: White Rock
white-rock-guide.verdict: White Rock suits middle-aged buyers, downsizers and young professionals. The catch is that some areas have a lot of stairs, parking can be a problem, and on some streets the power lines sit right in your view.

whonnock-guide.name: Whonnock
whonnock-guide.verdict: Whonnock suits buyers who want a rural setting and would trade a quick grocery run for a little more privacy. The catch is that you’ll still be driving for most errands.

willoughby-guide.name: Willoughby
willoughby-guide.verdict: Willoughby suits first-time buyers, commuters and growing families looking for new construction. The catch is smaller lots and street parking, and it can be busy during school hours.

yarrow-guide.name: Yarrow
yarrow-guide.verdict: Yarrow suits families who want a yard and like the idea of living in a small community. The catch is that living close enough to walk to school depends on the road you’re on.

yorkson-langley-guide.name: Yorkson
yorkson-langley-guide.verdict: Yorkson suits families who want a newer Willoughby street near the park and the middle school. The catch is most Willoughby Slope schools are already full, and the catchment map changes in September 2027, so check the address with SD35.

barnston-island-surrey-guide.name: Barnston Island
barnston-island-surrey-guide.verdict: Barnston Island suits farmers and buyers who want privacy on large rural parcels. The catch is that the island is low Fraser floodplain behind a dike.

works.t: Farmland and quiet: most of the island is in the Agricultural Land Reserve.
The ferry lands at Port Kells, close to Highway 1.

doesnt.t: The free ferry is the only access. It carries five vehicles at a time and runs within set hours.
School and shopping mean a crossing.

mt-lehman-abbotsford-guide.name: Mt Lehman
mt-lehman-abbotsford-guide.verdict: Mt Lehman suits acreage, hobby-farm and equestrian buyers who want a rural community with an elementary school. The catch is that ALR and local zoning rules can limit subdivision, suites and extra homes, and farm tax class has its own test tied to selling farm products.

works.t: An upland setting with a village core and Highway 1 access.
It sits above the Matsqui Prairie floodplain. Check parcels on the plateau edge one by one.

doesnt.t: No bus route runs through the village, and you drive to shop.
Water and sewer vary by property.

lindell-beach-bc-guide.name: Lindell Beach
lindell-beach-bc-guide.verdict: Lindell Beach suits recreational and second-home buyers who want the quieter south end of Cultus Lake. The catch is tenure.

works.t: Freehold options near the lake.
The original lots are fee simple, in the regional district’s water and sewer service areas. Confirm the connection lot by lot.

doesnt.t: No shops, schools or transit nearby.
Columbia Valley Road is the only way in and out, with summer traffic and the risk of flooding in heavy rain.

kent-bc-guide.name: Kent
kent-bc-guide.verdict: Kent suits buyers who want a small town with schools and recreation, and farmland nearby. The catch is that the Agassiz townsite sits on Fraser floodplain behind dikes and pumps.

works.t: Everyday needs in Agassiz: schools from kindergarten to grade 12, the recreation and aquatic centre and the library.
Harrison Hot Springs is next door.

doesnt.t: Not much transit, and not a wide range of shops.
Most major shopping means a drive to Chilliwack.

mount-currie-bc-guide.name: Mount Currie
mount-currie-bc-guide.verdict: Mount Currie suits Líl̓wat Nation members looking for housing through the Nation. Open-market buyers look at fee-simple homes in Pemberton or Pemberton Meadows. The catch is tenure.

works.t: The mountain setting, close to Pemberton.
The Nation runs its own school and learning centre.

doesnt.t: No full-service shopping or hospital in the community.
Pemberton is the nearest service centre.

whitby-estates-west-vancouver-guide.name: Whitby Estates
whitby-estates-west-vancouver-guide.verdict: Whitby Estates suits luxury buyers who want privacy, a large home and panoramic views. The catch is that covenants on title can require British Pacific Properties’ approval to build or alter, on top of District permits.

works.t: Views over Burrard Inlet, downtown and Stanley Park.
Chartwell Elementary and Sentinel Secondary are close by. Confirm the catchment for the address.

doesnt.t: Not walkable, and little transit: shopping is a drive.
Few sales, which makes pricing and resale timing harder to judge.

brunette-new-westminster-guide.name: Brunette
brunette-new-westminster-guide.verdict: Brunette suits detached-home buyers who want parks and SkyTrain close by and are fine living near industry. The catch is that lots by the river can face flood construction and stream setback rules.

works.t: Hume Park and the Brunette–Fraser Greenway.
Sapperton and Braid stations, Royal Columbian Hospital and Highway 1 are close.

doesnt.t: Warehouses, trucks and rail traffic shape the area.
Few listings: September 2026 had none listed and none sold.
